ig_carousel_topic.topic: The Kelly criterion — explained without the math degree
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
How much should you actually bet?
Most bettors guess. Kelly gives you a framework.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
The common mistake: flat-betting everything the same size regardless of edge.
A 52% win-rate play and a 58% win-rate play are not the same bet — sizing them identically throws away value and inflates risk.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Kelly's core idea: bet a fraction of your bankroll proportional to your edge.
Bigger edge = bigger bet. No edge = no bet.
It's not about being bold — it's about being calibrated.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Simple version: edge ÷ odds.
If you estimate 57% win probability on a -110 line (implied 52.4%), your edge is ~4.6%.
Full Kelly says bet about 4.6% of bankroll. Most sharps use half-Kelly (2.3%) to smooth variance.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
You don't need the formula memorized.
You need the mindset: size reflects confidence, not emotion.
Save this if you're still betting the same unit on every play regardless of edge.
